LESSON: CONSERVING WILD ANIMALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Conservation of Resources
Topic 1.3: Conserving Wild Animals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Conserving Wild Animals, part of Conservation of Resources in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: How can wild animals be kept away from crops and domestic animals?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Conserving Wild Animals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Patriotism: consciousness of social and moral duties to conserve wild animals and promote biodiversity.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Protection of biodiversity against extinction by deterring them without killing them.

Link to other subjects:

Learners relate conservation of wild animals through use of deterrents to knowledge on importance of wildlife learnt in social

studies.

Suggested learning resource

• Captioned video clips

• Resource person

• Print and non-print media

• Pictures of mesh fences, thorny fences, safe traps and innovative lights.
